name: Lotus Nikko Hotel Sravasti restaurant
why_it_matters: Lotus Nikko Sravasti's in-house multi-cuisine restaurant — walking distance from Sahet-Maheth (the Jetavana monastery where Buddha spent 24 monsoons). 60-room property built for the Japanese, Korean, Thai, Sri Lankan Buddhist pilgrim circuit; the kitchen runs the only East Asian menu in town.
insider_tip: Easily the most reliable sit-down meal in Sravasti — almost no independent restaurants exist. Reserve during pilgrim peak (Oct-Mar). Day-trippers from Lucknow can stop here for lunch.

name: Sri Lankan Pilgrim Rest House canteen
why_it_matters: Sri Lanka maintains a pilgrim rest house at Sahet-Maheth alongside other Buddhist nation rest houses (Korea, Thailand, Burma) — the in-house canteens serve simple meals to resident pilgrims and occasional walk-in visitors. Practical option for budget pilgrim travel along the Buddhist circuit.
insider_tip: Set meal times only; treat as a pilgrim rest-house canteen rather than a restaurant. Ask at the rest-house reception whether visitors are being served before sitting down.

name: Pawan Hotel restaurant
why_it_matters: Small hotel-attached restaurant in Sravasti town — useful budget alternative to the Lotus Nikko price point in a destination with almost no independent dining. Standard pure-veg north Indian thali kitchen.
insider_tip: Confirm operating hours by phone before walking over — small operations in Sravasti can close mid-afternoon during the off-pilgrim season (Apr-Sep).
